skill.description: Guide new Goldsky Turbo pipelines from requirements and dataset selection through YAML validation, approved deployment, and data flow checks.
skill.summary: Build blockchain data pipelines with explicit start positions, configured destinations, and validation before deployment.

security_audit.summary: All 75 static findings are false positives involving ordinary punctuation, Markdown formatting, pipeline configuration, or legitimate Goldsky operations. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or system reconnaissance. One semantic concern remains: hosted database provisioning lacks an explicit approval gate before creating account resources.

remediation.issue: Hosted database creation lacks an explicit user approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Before provisioning, explain plan requirements, resource ownership, and potential charges, then require explicit user approval for the selected project.

semantic_findings.title: Hosted Database Provisioning Lacks Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: The workflow offers hosted PostgreSQL creation when no database exists, without requiring approval before provisioning. This can create account resources with potential costs before the later pipeline deployment confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Provisioning appears before the explicit deployment approval step and has no equivalent confirmation requirement. Actual charges depend on the account plan and service terms.

content.user_title: Build and Deploy Goldsky Turbo Pipelines
content.value_statement: Blockchain data pipelines require clear source boundaries, destination settings, and validation before deployment. This skill guides those decisions and uses Goldsky commands to validate and deploy approved configurations.
actual_capabilities: Collect chain, dataset, destination, transform, and processing mode requirements.
Guide explicit start positions and chain-specific historical range filters.
Assemble pipeline YAML with dataset sources, optional transforms, and one or multiple sinks.
Guide destination secret checks and optional hosted PostgreSQL provisioning through Goldsky commands.
Run Goldsky validation, correct configuration issues, and present validated YAML for review.
Apply approved configurations and guide pipeline listing, inspection, and log checks.
limitations: Requires an installed Goldsky CLI, authenticated account, and appropriate project permissions for live operations.
Relies on related Goldsky skills for detailed dataset, transform, authentication, and sink configuration guidance.
Targets new pipelines rather than diagnosing existing failures or serving standalone wallet REST queries.
Validation does not guarantee sink capacity or runtime success; hosted PostgreSQL requires eligible access and separate provisioning approval.

use_cases.title: Stream Token Transfers
use_cases.description: Create a Base token transfer pipeline that writes new events into an application database from an agreed start position.

use_cases.title: Prepare Historical Analytics
use_cases.description: Define a bounded Ethereum backfill into ClickHouse, with source filters and a storage capacity review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Route Events to Multiple Destinations
use_cases.description: Configure one source with separate transform views for Kafka and webhook destinations, then validate and review the complete pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Define a First Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new Base ERC20 transfer pipeline into PostgreSQL. Ask for missing details and do not provision or deploy resources.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Streaming Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Build and validate YAML for Solana token transfers into my existing PostgreSQL destination. Confirm the start slot and secret name before writing it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bounded Backfill
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an Ethereum transaction backfill to ClickHouse between blocks [start] and [end]. Confirm capacity, use source filters, and validate before review.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Sink Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design one Base contract event pipeline with distinct transform views for Kafka and a webhook. Confirm decoding, start position, secrets, and destinations before validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced event decoding and destination routing

output_examples.input: Help me stream Base ERC20 transfers into my PostgreSQL database.
output: Please confirm whether ingestion starts now, at a historical block, or from full history.
Please provide the existing destination secret name, schema, and table.
Deployment remains pending configuration validation and your review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a full-history transfer backfill into a 512 MB PostgreSQL database.
output: Full-history ingestion can require days of replay and millions of rows.
A 512 MB destination is unsuitable for a large backfill.
Choose a narrower history range or a larger database before deployment.
No resources should be provisioned without your explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Send different views of one event source to Kafka and a webhook.
output: Proposed structure: one source, two transform views, and two independent sinks.
Each sink receives its corresponding transform output.
Confirm the source start position, Kafka secret, topic, and webhook destination before validation.

best_practices: Confirm the source start position and estimate destination capacity before generating a historical ingestion configuration.
Use existing secret references, verify the target project, and require explicit approval before provisioning hosted resources.
Validate the complete configuration, review every destination, and approve deployment only after checking the YAML.
anti_patterns: Omitting a source start position or selecting full history without checking storage requirements.
Treating successful validation as proof that a destination has enough capacity or that ingestion will succeed.
Provisioning hosted databases or applying pipeline configurations without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It guides new Goldsky Turbo blockchain data pipelines, including requirements, source selection, transforms, sinks, validation, and deployment.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Live commands require a suitable execution environment and Goldsky access.

faq.question: Which destinations does it cover?
faq.answer: The workflow covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, Pub/Sub, SQS, S3, and webhooks. Detailed settings rely on related Goldsky guidance.

faq.question: Can one pipeline use multiple destinations?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides multiple sinks from one source, with separate transform views where each destination needs different data.

faq.question: Will it deploy without review?
faq.answer: The documented deployment step requires YAML review and confirmation. Hosted database provisioning lacks an equivalent approval requirement and needs an additional explicit check.

faq.question: Does it debug existing pipelines?
faq.answer: No. Existing pipeline failures belong to the related turbo-doctor skill, while simple wallet REST lookups belong to feeds.
